question: rebuilt sizing with the scoring method as a facet: how much of the endpoint variance belongs to the condition
design: one fully crossed condition by method by element study per task, four conditions, two scoring methods, six anchor elements, one observation per cell. Elements are task specific, so the two tasks are analysed separately rather than pooled.

headline.elements_for_0_8_dependability: unreachable in both tasks within a cap of 400 elements

finding: the condition carries essentially none of the endpoint variance. In one task it is 0.9 percent of the clamped total and in the other the estimate is negative and clamps to zero. Element difficulty and residual dominate, at 47.9 and 37.1 percent in the first task and 50.5 percent residual in the second. Dependability as run is 0.040 and 0.000, and no element count within the search cap reaches 0.8 because more measurement cannot enlarge a signal estimated at zero.
consequence: the quality arm cannot be rescued by adding episodes. A block size was the wrong question; the endpoint as constructed does not separate conditions, so either the endpoint changes or no condition claim is available from it.
limits: four conditions give the condition component three degrees of freedom, so it is estimated very imprecisely
negative estimates in both tasks indicate components small relative to their sampling error, which is not the same as components known to be zero
one repeat per cell, so the residual absorbs the three-way interaction
eight artifacts on two tasks; this bounds the endpoint as measured here, not conditions in general
claim_scope: design validity evidence only; no treatment effect is claimed or denied
